interest: FBI surveillance of a Japanese man and his British wife in California, 1941.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.012881/1, spanning November 7 to December 24, 1941) consists of correspondence and investigative reports transmitted by FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover to Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr., concerning an investigation into suspected fraudulent passport activities by Japanese individuals in California. The inquiry focuses on Shigeo Ito (alias 'Mr. Ito'), who was accused by informant Lloyd Lawson Patterson of leading an illicit passport-dealing ring operating out of the Yamato Hotel in San Francisco. Through field investigations conducted by FBI agents in San Francisco and Los Angeles, aided by the Santa Ana District Attorney's Office, federal authorities tracked Ito and his English-born Caucasian wife to Laguna Beach, investigating his background as a former New York merchant, Christian peace lecturer, and alleged World War I White House worker, prompting passport index searches by the Department of State immediately after the outbreak of the Pacific War.
